record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.original_question: For an inner divisor G of L2_a(D), let Phi_G be the Green-potential function associated with |G|^2 - 1. Theorem 1.6 gives the isometry ||Gf||^2_L2 = ||f||^2_L2 + integral_D |f'(z)|^2 Phi_G(z) dS(z) for all f in the Hardy space H2(D). Does this isometry extend to every f in L2_a(D)? If it does not always extend, for exactly which inner divisors G does the extension hold?

evidence.quote: Theorem 1.6. If G is an inner divisor for L2_a(D), then the function Phi_G meets 0 ≤ Phi_G(z) ≤ 1 - |z|2, z ∈ D, and we have the isometry ... valid for all f ∈ H2(D).
Problem 1.7. Does the isometry in Theorem 1.6 extend to all f ∈ L2_a(D)? If not, then for which inner divisors G is this so?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk and let $dS$ denote normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. The Bergman space $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ consists of all holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ with $\|f\|_{L^2}^2=\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|^2\,dS(z)<\infty$, and the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{D})$ consists of holomorphic $f$ with $\sup_{0<r<1}\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|^2\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}<\infty$.

A function $G\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called an inner divisor for $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ if there exists a (closed, $z$-invariant) subspace $M\subset L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ such that $G$ is the extremal solution (of unit norm) to the corresponding extremal problem; equivalently, $G$ satisfies the orthogonality relation $\int_{\mathbb{D}}(|G(z)|^2-1)q(z)\,dS(z)=0$ for every bounded holomorphic $q$ in a natural class. For such a $G$, define the Green-potential function
$$\Phi_G(z)=\int_{\mathbb{D}}\log\Big|\frac{1-\bar w z}{z-w}\Big|^2\,(|G(w)|^2-1)\,dS(w),\qquad z\in\mathbb{D}.$$
It is known that $0\le \Phi_G(z)\le 1-|z|^2$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and that the isometry
$$\|Gf\|_{L^2}^2=\|f\|_{L^2}^2+\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f'(z)|^2\,\Phi_G(z)\,dS(z)$$
holds for every $f\in H^2(\mathbb{D})$.

Question: Does this isometry extend to every $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$? If it does not hold for all inner divisors $G$, characterize precisely those inner divisors $G$ of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ for which the identity above is valid for every $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the broader literature on contractive zero-divisors, biharmonic Green functions, and Bergman inner functions (Hedenmalm, Duren–Khavinson–Shapiro, Aleman–Richter–Sundberg, Olofsson, Shimorin), but did not turn up a definitive published resolution of the specific question of whether the $H^2$-isometry extends to all of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$, nor a precise characterization of the inner divisors for which the extension holds. Status appears unknown based on the available search evidence.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up survey on open problems in Bergman space theory; accessible content did not confirm a resolution of the extension question.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit confirmation that Problem 1.7 was resolved.

status_evidence.title: Contractive Zero-Divisors in Bergman Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Develops biharmonic Green-function methods for inner divisors but does not address extension of the H^2-isometry to all of L^2_a.
status_evidence.claim: Related techniques exist but the specific extension question is not settled.

status_evidence.title: An expansive multiplier property for operator-valued Bergman inner functions
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizations of Hedenmalm's contractive divisor result via biharmonic Green function methods.
status_evidence.claim: Related expansive/contractive results exist; explicit characterization for the isometry extension not found.
